We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x+7\, & ⟹\,v=\int (x+7)\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x-7\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-7x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
